newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.25 pct in range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.25 pct in range-bound trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted gains in subdued and selective trade on Monday, but brokers said prices were squeezed in narrow ranges although political tension cooled off after last week's 10.5 percent slump.

The IMKB National-100 closed 18 points, or 1.25 percent higher at 1,461 after moving in a tight range at between 1,443 and 1,466. Trade volume firmed to 23.14 trillion lira ($185.6 million) from Friday's 19.91 trillion ($160.1 million).
"Political tension faded as it was understood that the coalition government would go on," said Selcuk Ozcan from Aks securities.
"Privatisation hopes may enliven depending on the government's performance and first quarter profit prospects may move the market in coming days, but no major fluctuations are expected," he added.

Brokers said the market now awaited Thursday's cabinet meeting where measures to combat rising Islamist activism are expected to be discussed, following a National Security Council (MGK) statement on February 28 which urged action against what the army saw as rising Islamist zeal.
Tension which had mounted early last week due to a row between the coalition's Islamist wing and the secularist army eased considerably after Erbakan signed the MGK statement last Wednesday.
